text:
Katie: Hey team — enterprise POC with Acme Health is blocked. Their network rotates outbound proxy credentials every 24h and the TS SDK started getting 502/503s after rotation. Also seeing 429s when our client retries. Can we swarm? cc @Mike @Rana :eyes:
Mike: Ack. Do we have logs and which SDKs are affected (TS/Python)? Any reproducible steps?
Rana: I saw a quick capture from their test harness — it looks like the corporate forward proxy injects auth and when creds rotate long-lived connections get reset. TS streaming connections hold sockets open so when proxy sends 407/502 the connection gets killed and client sees ECONNRESET -> immediate retry -> they hit per-client rate limits (429). Short term: reduce keep-alive or add smarter retry with jitter/backoff. Also check HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY envs.
Jin: Can you paste the client config? e.g. they mentioned keepAlive=true and a 60s timeout.
Katie: Pasting sanitized logs from their debug run:
```
[2026-03-20T15:02:12Z] AcmeClient Error: 502 Bad Gateway (proxy)
  cause: Proxy Authentication Failed (407)
  stack: FetchError: request to https://api.redwood.ai/ failed, reason: socket hang up
  retries_attempted=3 backoff_ms=150
```
Rana: That 407 -> 502 path is classic. Recommendations:
- For TS Node: avoid long TCP keep-alive through proxy. Use an agent with keepAlive:false or set a short keepAliveTimeout.
- Add exponential backoff with jitter and cap (so retries don't convert 407s into 429s).
Suggested TS snippet:
```ts
import { HttpsProxyAgent } from 'https-proxy-agent';
const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent({ host: 'corp-proxy.local', port: 3128, keepAlive: false });
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  baseURL: 'https://api.redwood.ai',
  fetchOptions: { agent, timeout: 20000, retry: { retries: 4, factor: 2, minTimeout: 300 } }
});
```
Rana: And for Python customers using requests:
```py
import requests
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.util.retry import Retry
s = requests.Session()
s.trust_env = False  # avoid inherited proxy creds if they cause problems
s.proxies = {'http': 'http://proxy:3128', 'https': 'http://proxy:3128'}
retries = Retry(total=4, backoff_factor=0.5, status_forcelist=[429,502,503,504])
s.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retries))
```
Jin: Also ask the customer to add our egress IPs to their proxy allowlist or to configure a service-account style credential that can be rotated without changing the auth header principal. If they must rotate tokens, we should avoid letting sockets persist across rotation.
Olivia: SRE note: If credential rotation is frequent, we should assume degraded long-lived connections. Recommend setting short KV cache TTL for per-request proxy metadata and make our client re-auth on connection errors instead of blind retries. Also enable 503->fallback routing to a hosted fallback model if the dedicated path is flapping.
Mike: Quick commercial note — customer asked whether Dedicated/reserved capacity would avoid this. Answer: Dedicated can reduce noisy-neighbor throttling, but it won't bypass their corporate proxy. Recommend we propose a short-term config/workaround plus a longer-term Dedicated commit if they want guaranteed throughput. I'll handle commercial messaging.
Katie: Plan of attack: 1) Share the config snippets with customer now (TS + Python) 2) Ask them to test NO_PROXY for internal endpoints and/or add our egress IPs to allowlist 3) Offer a short maintenance window to coordinate credential rotation time with us so we can avoid POC bursts. Action items: Rana -> prepare small SDK patch to default to safer agent settings and cap retries; Jin -> write KB article and paste in POC thread; Mike -> follow up on Dedicated/pricing ask; Olivia -> confirm fallback routing options.
deploy-bot: Canary: TS SDK v1.4.2 deployed with proxy retry/timing tweaks. Monitor canary for 30m.
Katie: Thanks all — I'll message the customer with the snippets and schedule a sync. :thumbsup:
